A.title: What if your cat lived as long as you

seg: What if your cat lived *as long as you*?
You're seven. You get a kitten.
Fifteen. You're doing homework, and he falls asleep *right on your notebook*.
Twenty-two. Moving day. The first box he climbs into is now *his box*.
Thirty. He meets the love of your life. He's *jealous*.
A week later, he's asleep *on her lap*.
Thirty-five. A baby arrives. Whiskers *guards the crib* every night.
Fifty. You're both *going gray*. He still meets you at the door.
Eighty. You sit by the same window. He purrs. *Just like the first day*.
The oldest cat ever, Creme Puff, lived to *thirty-eight*.
Yours won't live that long. So *hug him today*.

B.title: What if your dog lived as long as you

seg: What if your dog lived *as long as you*?
You're six. A puppy comes home.
Dogs usually live *ten to thirteen years*.
But yours will be there *your whole life*.
Ten. He teaches you the most important rule: you walk *in any weather*.
Seventeen. Your first heartbreak. He doesn't understand words, but he puts *his head on your knees*.
Twenty-five. Your first job. Every evening he waits by the window, *at six sharp*.
Thirty. Your wedding. Who carries the rings? *Him, of course*.
Forty. Your kids fall asleep *curled up next to him*.
Seventy. You both walk slowly now. But that old ball is *still his favorite*.
The record for a dog is *twenty-nine years*. Bluey, a cattle dog from Australia.
Your friend has less time than that. So today, take *one extra walk*.

C.title: What if you could hear your cat's thoughts

seg: What if you could hear *your cat's thoughts*? Five a.m.
Human. The bowl is empty. This is a disaster.
This is on the edge. Let's test gravity.
Adult cats barely meow at each other. They save their meows *for humans*.
I learned your language. You never learned mine.
A slow blink is a *cat smile*.
You can't hunt at all. Here. Learn.
He kneads you with his paws, like kittens do *with their mom*.
I feel safe with you. Like when I was little.
I don't know what happened. But I'll lie right here. Until it passes.
He'll never say it out loud. But he thinks it *every single day*.

D.title: What if you could hear your dog's thoughts

seg: What if you could hear *your dog's thoughts*? You leave for work.
He's leaving. Forever. This is the end.
All day long, he *waits by the door*.
Is it now? How about now? Now?
He's back! Best day of my life!
His nose is *tens of thousands of times* better than yours.
You went to a café. You took the subway. And you petted another dog?!
The average dog understands about *a hundred and sixty-five words*.
But there's only one that matters. Walk!
At night, he *runs in his sleep*.
Running… running… almost got it… the ball…
I'll stay right here. As long as it takes. I'm in no hurry.
To you, he's part of your life. To him, you are *his whole life*.
